# anyscale_runtime_env_package (Resource)

Zips a local directory, uploads it to a cloud's storage bucket under a content-addressed name, and outputs its `uri` for a service's `runtime_env.working_dir` or `py_modules`. A plan shows an update only when included file contents, names, or exec bits change. Destroying it never deletes the uploaded object. Supports AWS and GCP clouds, not Azure. See the [Runtime Environment Packages guide](../guides/runtime-env-packages.md).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Package ./app and deploy it as a service's working_dir. Editing a
# file under ./app plans an update to the package and a rollout of the
# service; an unchanged tree (even a fresh clone) plans nothing.
resource "anyscale_runtime_env_package" "app" {
  source_dir = "${path.module}/app"
  # The cloud of the compute config the service runs on.
  cloud_id = "cld_abc123"

  # Added to .git, .venv, venv, __pycache__ and any .gitignore rules.
  excludes = ["tests/"]
}

resource "anyscale_service" "example" {
  name              = "my-service"
  build_id          = "cenv_abc123"
  compute_config_id = "cpt_abc123"

  ray_serve_config = {
    applications = [
      {
        import_path = "main:app"
        runtime_env = {
          working_dir = anyscale_runtime_env_package.app.uri
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}

output "package_uri" {
  value       = anyscale_runtime_env_package.app.uri
  description = "Storage URI of the uploaded package"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cloud_id` (String) Cloud whose storage receives the package. Use the cloud of the compute config that runs it: another cloud's cluster may not be able to read the object, which fails only when the service starts.
- `source_dir` (String) Local directory to package, typically under `path.module`. Read on every plan. Its location does not affect `content_hash`.

### Optional

- `cloud_resource_ids` (List of String) Cloud resources to upload to. Defaults to the cloud's primary resource. List every resource a multi-resource compute config uses, and reference `relative_path` instead of `uri`.
- `excludes` (List of String) Extra `.gitignore`-style patterns, relative to `source_dir`, to leave out. Always excluded: `.git`, `.venv`, `venv`, `__pycache__`, and anything a `.gitignore` in the tree ignores.

### Read-Only

- `content_hash` (String) SHA-256 of the included files' relative paths, contents, and exec bits. Modification times are ignored, so a fresh checkout of the same code plans no change.
- `id` (String) Same as `relative_path`.
- `relative_path` (String) Object key of the package, identical in every target bucket. Use it as `relative_working_dir` when the compute config spans several cloud resources.
- `uri` (String) Storage URI of the package (`s3://...` or `gs://...`) in the first target bucket. Use it as `working_dir`.
